challenges.name: replay-detection-evidence
challenges.title: Replay detection: read the rows and the log
challenges.description: Two statements on real refresh_tokens rows and API logs: what to revoke when a rotated token comes back, and when a reuse is only a network retry.

questions.question:
Family f_12 after an alert (refresh tokens rotate on every refresh):

SELECT id, device_id, used_at, revoked_at, replaced_by
FROM refresh_tokens WHERE family_id = 'f_12' ORDER BY created_at;

 id   | device_id | used_at             | revoked_at | replaced_by
 r_40 | phone-31  | 2026-10-20 08:00:05 |            | r_41
 r_41 | phone-31  | 2026-10-20 08:15:09 |            | r_42
 r_42 | phone-31  |                     |            |

API log:
2026-10-20 08:31:44 POST /auth/refresh token_id=r_40 device=phone-31 ip=203.0.113.50 reuse=true

Statement: "Revoking only r_40, the token that was presented again, is enough: r_42 is the phone's current token, so it is safe to leave it valid."
questions.explanation: False. r_40 came back about 31 minutes after it was rotated (and after a second rotation), so at least two parties held a copy of it. The server cannot tell who performed the rotations r_40 -> r_41 -> r_42: if an attacker stole r_40 and refreshed first, the attacker holds r_42 and the learner is the one presenting r_40 now; it could also be the other way round. r_40 is already useless (it is used), so revoking it alone changes nothing. The safe answer is to revoke the whole family, r_42 included, record a security event and let the real learner sign in again. The misconception is that whoever presents the old token must be the attacker.

questions.question:
API log, one phone with a 2 s client timeout:

10:00:00.000 POST /auth/refresh device=phone-8812 token_id=r_77 -> 200 rotated, issued r_78
10:00:02.000 client: request timed out, retrying
10:00:02.410 POST /auth/refresh device=phone-8812 token_id=r_77

Config: REFRESH_GRACE_MS=10000. At 10:00:02.410, r_77 has used_at 10:00:00.000 and replaced_by r_78; r_78 has used_at NULL and revoked_at NULL.

Statement: "With this grace window, the retry receives the refresh token already issued as r_78, no new row is inserted, and no security event is recorded."
questions.explanation: True. The reuse comes from the same device 2.41 s after r_77 was used, inside the 10 s window, and the successor r_78 has not been used or revoked, so this looks like a lost response, not a second party. The server answers with the successor it already issued (kept for the window), so the family does not fork and the phone ends up with the one live token. Two misconceptions: that every reuse must revoke the family (every slow network would sign learners out), and that a retry should get a brand-new token (that creates a second live branch in the family).

challenges.name: refresh-token-replay-detection
challenges.title: Replay Detection: Revoke the Family
challenges.description:
CodeDev rotates the refresh token on every POST /auth/refresh, but when a token that was already rotated comes back, the API only answers 401 and leaves the rest of the family alive. A copy stolen from a learner's laptop was used once more after the learner had rotated it, and the attacker's own chain kept working. Write refresh(store, req) with replay detection.

Look the row up by sha256(token) (hex, helper given). Check in this order: (1) no row -> {status:"invalid"}; (2) revokedAt set -> {status:"revoked"}; (3) req.now >= expiresAt -> {status:"expired"}; (4) unused row -> claim it with store.markUsed (a compare-and-swap: UPDATE ... SET used_at = $2 WHERE id = $1 AND used_at IS NULL AND revoked_at IS NULL RETURNING *), issue the successor in the same family for the row's user and device with store.issue, link it with store.recordSuccessor and return {status:"rotated", token}; if issue returns null (family revoked) return {status:"revoked"}; (5) used row (a reuse) -> grace when the request comes from the row's device, less than GRACE_MS = 10000 ms after usedAt (10000 ms is outside), and the successor row (replacedBy) is neither used nor revoked: return {status:"grace", token: store.getReply(row.id)}, the successor already issued, and create nothing. Any other reuse is a replay: revoke the whole family with store.revokeFamily, record one security event {type:"refresh_token_reuse", userId, familyId, tokenId: the presented row id, deviceId: req.deviceId, at: req.now} and return {status:"replay_detected"}.

Input: {"steps": [...], "quiet"?: true}; a step is {op:"login", user, device, at} (a new family) or {op:"refresh", token, device, at}, where token is a label ("t3" = the token of row r3) or a literal string. Times are milliseconds on a fake clock; tokens live 14 days. Output: one line per step ("refresh t1 laptop @3600000: replay_detected", "... rotated t2"), then one line per security event and one per row ("r1 f1 phone used=60000 revoked=- next=r2"); with quiet, a summary instead of the step and row lines.
hints: When a token that was already rotated comes back, can the server tell which of the two callers is the real learner? If not, which tokens of the family could the other caller be holding right now?

Everything you need for a reuse is on the presented row and its successor: row.usedAt (when the window started), row.deviceId, row.replacedBy (load it with store.findById to see whether it was used) and store.getReply(row.id). Check the cheap grace conditions first and let everything else fall through to the alarm.

A similar rule on different data: a one-time sign-in link c1 is used at 12:00:00 and creates session s2. The same browser opens c1 again at 12:00:03 while s2 is untouched: show s2 again and create nothing. Another browser opens c1, or s2 was already used, or it is 12:00:30: end every session that came from c1 and log one alert with the link id, the browser and the time.

tests.name: Reuse from another device after rotation revokes the whole family
tests.expected:
login u_8812 phone: t1
refresh t1 phone @60000: rotated t2
refresh t1 laptop @3600000: replay_detected
refresh t2 phone @3660000: revoked
event refresh_token_reuse user=u_8812 family=f1 token=r1 device=laptop at=3600000
r1 f1 phone used=60000 revoked=3600000 next=r2
r2 f1 phone used=- revoked=3600000 next=-
